product.title: terrain: hillshade and land cover tint tiles

standing.claim: A truncated land cover answer with HTTP 200 crashes the build and the verify re-fetch, which breaks D16 (one tile's failure is that tile's only).
standing.evidence: check_land_tiff decodes the palette outside the _open wrapper (line 414: np.unique(np.asarray(im))), so Pillow's 'image file is truncated' OSError is not a TerrainError. fetch_checked catches only TerrainError (line 488), and so do the source_bytes catches (lines 524 and 537) and _tile_job (line 598). _refetch_compare (line 1070) catches only TerrainError too, so verify crashes. Reproduced: a zoom 5 build() with one half-length answer for tile 5/5/10 raised OSError out of build(); fetch_checked and _tile_job raised the same error; verify's re-fetch raised it as well. Under the job's failure branch (docstring lines 73-75) both layers would be marked unavailable for the whole run. No test covers a truncated image (TriesTests, lines 289-347).
standing.fix: In check_land_tiff, wrap the decode in try/except Exception and raise TerrainError('the land cover answer is not a readable image'). In fetch_checked, treat any Exception from check as a failed try. Catch Exception, not only TerrainError, around source_bytes in _tile_job (lines 595-599), around the cache check at line 523, and around the fetch in _refetch_compare (lines 1061-1071). Add tests: a half-length TIFF with status 200 is tried three times, the tile is listed missing, and the build finishes partial; a verify re-fetch of such a body reports a failed re-fetch and does not raise.

standing.claim: The full suite exits 1 on the final working tree, which breaks the brief's rule that the whole suite stays green.
standing.evidence: Six failures, all in tests/test_website_workflow.py PushPathsCoverTheTests: test_every_website_test_module_is_a_push_path (lines 211-214) for test_basemap2, test_history_layers, test_labels, test_landmarks and test_terrain ('tests/test_terrain.py is not in on.push.paths'), and test_every_website_test_module_runs_in_the_offline_line (lines 216-218). The terrain tests themselves pass (57 OK). The builder's measurements.json records the same failure set. website.yml is not on P1's file list, so the builder cannot make this edit.
standing.fix: The integrator adds tests/test_terrain.py, together with the other new test modules, to on.push.paths (the list at lines 27-38 and below) and to the offline unittest line in website.yml, then re-runs the full suite. Until that edit lands the branch is red and must not be reported green.

standing.claim: When the shading date is missing, the words say 'data as of unknown', and the credits print for both layers whether or not they loaded. AGENTS.md rule 5 requires 'Data unavailable' for a missing input.
standing.evidence: map_data() and describe() both fall back to 'unknown' (lines 1104 and 1082), and the credits dict at line 1109 is built regardless of layer state. Reproduced with state partial and shading_date None: map_data()['credits']['shading'] reads 'Terrain shading: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP) hillshade, data as of unknown. 3DEP data courtesy of the U.S. Geological Survey.' while the shading layer is unavailable. That state is reachable: build() marks layer h unavailable when the service description cannot be read and no cached copy exists (lines 729-733), and the land layer can still load. The credit therefore claims a source is in use when it is not.
standing.fix: When shading_date is missing or layer h is not loaded, print 'Terrain shading: Data unavailable in this update.' with no date (sentence template at lines 185-186). Print each layer's credit only when that layer has files. Add a test with shading_date None and layer h unavailable.

standing.claim: check_shading_png reads only the header, so a truncated 256 px PNG passes, is cached as a checked answer, and is not requested again until --refresh.
standing.evidence: check_shading_png (lines 397-403) tests the signature, the mode and the size only; _open is lazy. source_bytes then writes the copy (line 546). On a zoom 5 build with one half-length PNG for 5/5/10, the request was made once, the draw failed (the tile is missing, and the failure is caught at lines 601-603), and the file stayed in the cache. A second run with a healthy source made zero requests for that tile, and the block still lists it missing (layers.h.missing = ['5/5/10']). The tile is honestly shown as paper, but the bad copy persists until the next as-of month or a --refresh.
standing.fix: Fully decode in the check (call im.load() inside check_shading_png) so a truncated answer fails the try and is requested again. Add a test in which a truncated PNG is requested again on the next run.

standing.claim: The docstring says the service's no-data grey value (its PNG transparency value) becomes 255. In the live answers 253 is an ordinary hillshade level, so the remap changes real pixels and its stated rationale is unsupported.
standing.evidence: shading_jpeg reads the transparency value and maps every pixel equal to it to 255 (lines 442-444; docstring lines 33-34). All 881 cached shading answers carry transparency 253 (probe over /home/user/hail-b5/out/b6/cache/P1/shading/2026-09). In 291 of them pixels equal 253 (tile 10/182/354 has 145), so the remap turns those real values into 255. The effect is two grey levels, which is not visible, so I rate it low. Raise it to medium if a changed stored value counts as a wrong number for this product. The test that enshrines the remap is at tests/test_terrain.py line 243.
standing.fix: Drop the remap, or keep it only with a test that shows where the service really returns no-data. Correct the docstring and rename the test.

standing.claim: The docstring presents the palette as the proof's colours per code. Code 71 is #eaf0dc in the proof, but the class uses 52's #e6ecd6; code 81 is #f0efd9 in the proof, but the class uses 82's #f2efd0.
standing.evidence: TINT (lines 138-143) uses one colour per class by design; the docstring (lines 36-40) lists the codes with the class colour but does not say the class takes its first code's colour. The proof table is /home/user/hail-b5/out/b6/cartography/render/proof_render.py lines 74-76 (71: '#eaf0dc', 81: '#f0efd9'). The forest, developed (22), crop (82) and water colours match the proof exactly.
standing.fix: Say in the docstring that each class takes the colour of its first listed code (52, 82, 22, 11, 41), or choose the class colours deliberately and record why.

standing.claim: _detail prints 'did not load after 3 tries' for every missing tile, including tiles refused without a retry and tiles stopped by the deadline.
standing.evidence: fetch_checked raises TerrainError with tries=0 for non-retried statuses (line 495), and source_bytes raises the deadline reason with tries=0 (line 534). _detail (line 802) ignores both and always prints the try count.
standing.fix: Keep each tile's reason (or its tries) with the missing key, and print that reason in detail.

standing.claim: Running build without --cache from the repository root creates an untracked terrain-cache folder in the worktree.
standing.evidence: The default is the relative path 'terrain-cache'. /home/user/wt/wt-b6/.gitignore lists address-cache, hail-cache and joins-cache, but not terrain-cache.
standing.fix: Make --cache required, or default it to a path outside the repository. If the default stays, add the folder to .gitignore.

standing.claim: A run with --zooms 8, or any subset, deletes the layer's files for all other zooms and rewrites the block for the subset with no warning.
standing.evidence: build() removes the whole h or l folder before building (lines 726-728), and the mirror then lists only the built zooms. Found by reading the code; not run.
standing.fix: Refuse a subset unless --keep-other-zooms is given, or keep the other zooms' entries. The monthly job must always pass 5-10.

standing.claim: Without --refresh the cached service description is reused indefinitely, so the shading as-of month and the cache key do not advance. The land cover as-of is a constant, not read from the service.
standing.evidence: _shading_meta passes refresh through to source_bytes (line 566), which returns a cached copy that passes its check before any request (lines 527-528). The description cache has no expiry. LAND_AS_OF (line 131) is hard-coded from the 20230630 keyword.
standing.fix: The monthly job must pass --refresh, and integration.md should say so. Read the land cover date at each build, or check it and fail loudly when the layer name changes.

standing.claim: Old as-of months stay in the cache forever. About 31 MB accumulates per month, so the 1 GB product limit is reached in roughly 30 months.
standing.evidence: The shading cache path includes the as-of month (line 585). The measured cache is 90 MB for one month (31 MB shading, 59 MB land cover). Nothing deletes older as-of folders.
standing.fix: After a successful build, delete the cache folders of other as-of months.

standing.claim: Integration hazard: every B6 product rewrites hail/index.json and hail/manifest.json without a lock, and _read_base_index discards the whole base index when its format string differs. Products run together could lose entries, and a product with a different format string would drop the others' keys.
standing.evidence: _store_block (lines 836-854) reads, changes and rewrites both shared files. _read_base_index returns only {'f': ...} when the format string differs (lines 817-819).
standing.fix: The integrator runs the store writers one after another in the job. Every product uses the same base index format string and writes only its own keys.
